mainTopic: The decree against סדין בציצית, which garments need ציצית, and 'תעשה ולא מן העשוי'
overview: The amud opens by searching for the reason the חכמים forbade ציצית with wool תכלת on a linen garment. A קל וחומר knocks down an earlier reason. רבא then explains the worry: a torn linen garment might be sewn with linen thread near the corner, and that thread later used as ציצית, which is invalid because of 'תעשה ולא מן העשוי'. רב זירא adds a second worry about a nighttime garment. רבא rules that a garment made of cloth and leather follows its main body, while רב אחאי follows the corner. רב הונא rules that ציצית tied onto a three-cornered garment before it became four-cornered are פסול. The גמרא tests this against the early חסידים and against רבי זירא's case of tying ציצית onto a garment that already has them. רבא and רב פפא argue over that second challenge. Finally שמואל rules that תכלת is not subject to כלאים even on an exempt garment, and the גמרא begins asking which garment counts as exempt. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If we rely on letters for כרת matters, surely we can for ציצית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the previous explanation for the decree. We rely on letters from the court even for חמץ on פסח and for יום הכפורים, which carry כרת, so we can surely rely on them for ציצית, which is only a positive מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For חמץ on פסח and for יום הכפורים, which carry כרת, we rely on the letters sent by the court. Here, where it is only a positive commandment, is it not all the more so?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pushing away the earlier suggested reason for the decree, using a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier reason depended on a worry that people could not rely on letters or reports from the court. But the most serious laws, which carry כרת, already depend on those letters. So a mere עשה like ציצית surely can too, and that reason falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: A severe heavenly punishment, being 'cut off'
We rely on
Letters or official notices sent by the court
Merely a positive commandment
All the more so, a קל וחומר argument

phrases.english: Leavened bread on Passover and Yom Kippur
which carry karet, we rely on letters;
phrases.notes: These are letters from the court in ארץ ישראל telling everyone when the month began, so people know which day is the holiday.

phrases.english: here, which is merely a positive commandment,
is it not all the more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: חמץ בפסח ויום הכפורים דכרת סמכינן אדיסקי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the explanation for the decree that was suggested just before this point in the daf.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The previous reason given for the decree against סדין בציצית
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes we cannot rely on court letters, yet we rely on them even for כרת-level laws, so surely we can for a simple עשה.

steps.title: רבא's reason: a torn linen garment sewn with linen thread
steps.stepSummary: רבא offers a new reason, also reported in ארץ ישראל in the name of רבי זירא. A person might tear his linen garment within three fingerbreadths of the corner, sew it with linen thread, and then use that thread as ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: I said this idea, and in the West (ארץ ישראל) it was also said in the name of רבי זירא, agreeing with me. The worry is that his linen garment might tear within three fingerbreadths of the corner, and he will sew it up.
steps.whatsHappening: After the old reason fell, רבא gives a new explanation for the decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that thread put there to repair a tear could later be used as ציצית. The next step explains why that is a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The West,' meaning ארץ ישראל
Like me, in agreement with my view
His linen sheet or garment
Lest, perhaps (expresses the worry behind a decree)

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
This matter, I said it,
and it was stated in the West
in the name of Rabbi Zeira, like me:
lest his linen garment tear within three
phrases.notes: Three fingerbreadths from the corner, the area where the ציצית are tied.

phrases.english: and he sew it up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא אמר רבא הא מילתא אמרי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reason that was rejected in step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree was based on the reason that step 1 rejected.
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree comes from the worry that linen repair thread near the corner will end up being used as ציצית.

steps.title: ציצית must be made for the מצוה, not taken from what is already there
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'תעשה' teaches that ציצית must be made for the מצוה. Using thread that is already attached for repair is invalid, so the person would be wearing plain כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Torah said: 'You shall make,' and not from what is already made.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the Torah source that explains why the repair thread would be a real problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinarily ציצית with תכלת on linen is permitted, because the מצוה overrides כלאים. But if the threads are invalid as ציצית, the מצוה does not apply. Then the wool and linen are simply forbidden שעטנז.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall make,' the threads must be made for the מצוה
Not from something already made or attached

steps.confusionAlert: The decree is not saying that ציצית on a linen garment are invalid by Torah law. The concern is a specific case where invalid thread turns the garment into forbidden כלאים.

phrases.english: And the Torah said: "You shall make"
and not from what is already made.

steps.triggerLanguage: והתורה אמרה תעשה ולא מן העשוי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the scenario in step 2 is a real problem.
steps.raayaObject: That ציצית made from repair thread are invalid

steps.title: רבי זירא removes the ציצית from his linen garment
steps.stepSummary: Because of this decree, רבי זירא untied the ציצית from his own linen garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא untied his linen garment, taking off its ציצית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports what רבי זירא actually did in practice because of the decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the decree was followed in real life by the same sage whose name was attached to רבא's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Untied, loosened (here: removed the ציצית)

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira untied his linen garment.
phrases.notes: He means he took the ציצית off the garment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the practical application of the reason given in steps 2 and 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, one removes ציצית from a linen garment because of the decree.

steps.title: A second reason: a nighttime garment
steps.stepSummary: רב זירא adds that the decree is also because of כסות לילה. A person might put ציצית on a garment worn at night, where the מצוה does not apply, and end up wearing plain כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זירא said: The decree is also because of a nighttime garment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זירא adds a second reason for the same decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ציצית apply only to daytime clothing. On a nighttime garment there is no מצוה to override כלאים, so wool on linen there would simply be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a protective fence
Also
A nighttime garment, which is exempt from ציצית

steps.whatToRemember: The decree against סדין בציצית has two reasons. First, linen repair thread might be used as invalid ציצית (רבא and רבי זירא). Second, there is the worry about a nighttime garment (רב זירא). In both cases the מצוה would not apply, leaving forbidden כלאים.

phrases.english: Rav Zeira said:
The decree is also because of a nighttime garment.

steps.triggerLanguage: רב זירא אמר גזירה נמי משום כסות לילה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second reason alongside רבא's reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The decree also guards against putting ציצית with wool on a linen nighttime garment, where no מצוה applies.

steps.title: A garment of cloth and leather follows its main body
steps.stepSummary: רבא, backed by a report from ארץ ישראל in the name of רבי זירא, rules that a cloth garment with leather corners needs ציצית. A leather garment with cloth corners is פטור. The reason is that the main body of the garment must be cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: I said this ruling, and in ארץ ישראל they reported the same in the name of רבי זירא. A cloth garment with leather corners needs ציצית. A leather garment with cloth corners does not. Why? Because the main part of the garment has to be cloth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new rule for a garment made partly of cloth and partly of leather. He says we look at what the main body of the garment is made of.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leather garments do not need ציצית, but cloth garments do. When a garment mixes the two, רבא says the deciding factor is the body, not the corners. So cloth body means חייב, and leather body means פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means woven cloth, as opposed to leather
Leather
Its corners, the place where ציצית are tied
The main part, the body of the garment
Obligated / exempt

phrases.english: And Rava said: This is a statement I said,
and it was stated in the West
phrases.notes: 'The West' means ארץ ישראל, which lies west of בבל.

phrases.english: in the name of Rabbi Zeira, in line with my view:

phrases.aramaic: הִיא שֶׁל בֶּגֶד וּכְנָפֶיהָ שֶׁל עוֹר – חַיֶּיבֶת,
phrases.english: If it is of cloth and its corners are of leather, it is obligated;

phrases.aramaic: הִיא שֶׁל עוֹר וּכְנָפֶיהָ שֶׁל בֶּגֶד – פְּטוּרָה.
phrases.english: if it is of leather and its corners are of cloth, it is exempt.
What is the reason? We require the main part to be cloth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new rule from רבא on a related ציצית topic: which garments are obligated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mixed cloth and leather garment follows its main body. Cloth body means חייב, and leather body means פטור.

steps.title: רב אחאי goes by the corner
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי disagrees and decides by what the corners are made of.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a different opinion. רב אחאי decides the garment's status by the material of its corners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב אחאי the outcome flips. Cloth corners on a leather body would be חייב, and leather corners on a cloth body would be פטור. The reason is that ציצית are tied on the corners, as the פסוק says 'על כנפי בגדיהם'.

keyTerms.meaning: Corner of the garment
Goes after, decides according to

phrases.english: Rav Aḥai follows the corner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing view to רבא's rule in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The material of the corner decides whether the garment needs ציצית.

steps.title: ציצית tied on before the fourth corner was added are invalid
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that if someone tied ציצית onto a three-cornered garment and then made it four-cornered, the ציצית are פסול. This is because of 'תעשה ולא מן העשוי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב סחורה, who said it in the name of רב הונא: If someone tied ציצית onto a garment with three corners and then made it into a four-cornered garment, the ציצית are invalid. The Torah says 'make', which means not from something already made.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule. ציצית that were tied on when the garment did not yet need them do not count later, once the garment becomes obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A three-cornered garment is פטור from ציצית, so tying them on then was not doing the מצוה. The word 'תעשה' requires the ציצית to be made when there is an obligation. Strings that were already there before do not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Attached, tied on the ציצית
A garment with only three corners, which is exempt
Invalid
'Make it', and not from what is already made

steps.confusionAlert: The ציצית are not invalid because of how they were tied. They are invalid because they were tied on when the garment had no obligation yet.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב סְחוֹרָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Seḥora said that Rav Huna said:
If one attached ritual fringes to a garment with three corners,
and then completed it to four corners, it is invalid,
because it says “Make” and not from what is already made.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב סְחוֹרָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the timing of attaching ציצית compared with when the garment becomes obligated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ציצית attached before the garment was obligated are פסול, because of תעשה ולא מן העשוי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that ציצית must be attached when the garment already has the obligation.

steps.title: The early חסידים tied on תכלת while still weaving
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the early חסידים tied on תכלת once three fingerbreadths had been woven. That seems to be before the garment was obligated, which contradicts רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא objects: the early pious men, once they had woven three fingerbreadths of the garment, would tie תכלת onto it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא from a ברייתא about the early חסידים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After only three fingerbreadths of weaving, the garment is far from finished and is not yet obligated. Yet these pious people tied on ציצית right then, and surely they did it properly. This seems to show that ציצית tied on before the obligation are valid.

keyTerms.meaning: The early pious men
They wove
The sky-blue thread of ציצית

phrases.english: They raised an objection: The early pious men,
once they wove three fingerbreadths of it,
would attach sky-blue thread to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's rule from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that ציצית attached before the obligation are פסול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חסידים attached תכלת to an unfinished garment that was not yet obligated. This implies such ציצית are valid.

steps.title: Read it as three fingerbreadths left to weave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא. It means the חסידים tied on תכלת when only three fingerbreadths remained to be woven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: once they had finished the garment except for three fingerbreadths, they would tie תכלת onto it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing one word in the ברייתא, so that it describes a garment that is almost finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'שארגו' (they wove three) becomes 'שפצעו' (they finished up to three). Now the garment is nearly complete and already big enough to count as a garment. So the חסידים were not tying ציצית onto something that was far from obligated, and רב הונא's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say', meaning read the text this way instead
They finished, leaving only a little left to weave

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's rule stands: ציצית must be attached when there is an obligation. The story of the חסידים refers to a garment that was almost finished.

phrases.english: Say instead: once they completed it up to three fingerbreadths,
phrases.notes: He means only three fingerbreadths were left to weave.

phrases.english: they would attach sky-blue thread to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the reading of the ברייתא (אימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חסידים tied תכלת onto a barely started garment, before it was obligated.
steps.terutzMaskana: They tied it on when the garment was almost finished, with only three fingerbreadths left to weave.

steps.title: Challenge from tying ציצית onto a garment that already has them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רב הונא's rule. רבי זירא said that ציצית tied onto a garment that already had ציצית are כשרה, even though they were not needed at that moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really say 'make it, and not from what is already made'? Is that so? But רבי זירא said: if someone tied ציצית onto a garment that already had ציצית, they are kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's rule. It brings a case where ציצית were tied on when they were not needed, and they are still kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי זירא's case the garment already had ציצית, so the second set was extra when it was tied on. Later the first set is removed, and the second set is kosher. That looks just like ציצית tied on before there was a requirement, which רב הונא said is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: He attached ציצית onto a garment that already had ציצית attached
Kosher, valid
Is that so? (a word that opens a challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא's case is not about a three-cornered garment. It is about a fully obligated garment that gets a second, extra set of ציצית. The comparison is only that both sets of ציצית were tied on when they were not needed.

phrases.english: And do we really say: 'You shall make' — and not from what is already made?
Is that so?
phrases.notes: This word is in round brackets, so some versions leave it out.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Zeira say:
If one attached ritual fringes onto a garment that already had them attached, they are kosher.
phrases.notes: He means the first set is later taken off, and the second set stays kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמְרִינַן תַּעֲשֶׂה וְלֹא מִן הֶעָשׂוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא was reread in Step 10, the גמרא brings a new challenge to רב הונא's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule (Step 8) that ציצית tied on before the garment was obligated are פסול because of תעשה ולא מן העשוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי זירא allows ציצית that were tied on when they were not needed, since the garment already had ציצית. So tying on ציצית without a requirement should not make them פסול.

steps.title: רבא: a second set that breaks בל תוסיף is not a real act
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the difference. Tying a second set onto a garment that already has ציצית breaks the rule of בל תוסיף. A forbidden tying like that does not count as an act of making ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Now that he is breaking 'do not add,' it is not considered an act.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge from רבי זירא. He shows that רבי זירא's case is different from רב הונא's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rashi explains: since tying the second set breaks a Torah rule, it does not count as an act of making ציצית. Their real making happens only when the first set is cut off, so they are not 'from what is already made.' In רב הונא's case, tying ציצית onto a three-cornered garment breaks no rule, so it does count as an act, and those ציצית were made before the garment needed them.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition against adding to a מצוה
An act, a real action that counts
Now, since (used to build a logical point)

phrases.english: Rava said:
Now, since he stands in violation of 'do not add',
it is not considered an act.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא בְּבַל תּוֹסִיף קָאֵי מַעֲשֶׂה לָא הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 11 and defends רב הונא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: tying the extra set breaks בל תוסיף, so it does not count as an act of making; tying on a three-cornered garment breaks no rule, so it does count.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases involve ציצית tied on when not required, so they should be judged the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: Tying ציצית in a way that breaks בל תוסיף does not count as making them. The second set is made only when the first set is cut off, so it is not 'from what is already made' and is כשר. Tying onto a three-cornered garment breaks no rule, so it counts as making the ציצית too early, and they are פסול.

steps.title: רב פפא: maybe he meant to cancel the first set
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא objects to רבא. Maybe רבי זירא is talking about someone who meant to cancel the first set. Then there is no בל תוסיף at all, yet his act still counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objected: How do we know the man meant to add? Maybe he meant to cancel the first set. Then there is no 'do not add,' yet there is still an act!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks רבא's answer. רבא's reason depends on בל תוסיף, and רבי זירא's case might have no בל תוסיף at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the person tied the second set intending to replace the first set, he is not adding anything, so בל תוסיף does not apply. Without בל תוסיף, the tying does count as an act, so the second set would be 'from what is already made.' Yet רבי זירא still calls those ציצית כשרה. That means רבא's answer does not explain רבי זירא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it (challenged the previous answer)
To add
To cancel, to nullify
Perhaps, maybe

phrases.english: Rav Pappa objected to this:
From where do we know that the man intended to add?
Perhaps he intended to cancel the first set,
and there is no 'do not add', yet there is an act!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא מִמַּאי דְּגַבְרָא לְאוֹסוֹפֵי קָא מִיכַּוֵּין
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's answer that tying the extra set counts as an act because it breaks בל תוסיף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי זירא's case may be about someone who meant to replace the first set. Then there is no בל תוסיף, but the ציצית are still kosher. So רבא's reason cannot be what makes the act count.

steps.title: שמואל: תכלת is not subject to כלאים, even on an exempt garment
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that ציצית with תכלת do not break the rule of כלאים. This is true even when they are on a garment that is פטור from ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב מתנא, in the name of שמואל: תכלת is not subject to the rule of כלאים, and this is so even on a garment that is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from שמואל about ציצית and כלאים. It still deals with ציצית tied on where they are not strictly required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the תורה allows ציצית to be an exception to כלאים. שמואל says this exception holds even on a garment that is פטור from ציצית, where you might think there is no מצוה to allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: Sky-blue dyed wool strings used in ציצית
The prohibition of mixing wool and linen in a garment (שעטנז)
A garment that is exempt from ציצית

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the exception of ציצית from כלאים can apply even where the garment itself has no obligation of ציצית.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב מַתְנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav Mattana said that Shmuel said:
Tekhelet is not subject to the prohibition of diverse kinds,
and this is so even on a garment that is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב מַתְנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל תְּכֵלֶת אֵין בָּהּ מִשּׁוּם כִּלְאַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the back-and-forth over רבי זירא's ruling, the גמרא brings a new related statement about ציצית and כלאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ציצית with תכלת do not break the rule of כלאים, even on a garment that is פטור from ציצית.

steps.title: Which garment counts as exempt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what שמואל meant by a טלית that is פטור from ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by an exempt cloak?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about one phrase in שמואל's ruling: what kind of cloak is 'exempt' from ציצית? This question sets up the next move, where the גמרא will try out possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל allowed ציצית with תכלת on a garment that is פטור, even though wool and linen together would normally be כלאים. To understand his ruling, we first need to know exactly which garment he is talking about. The answer will show how far his rule reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: A cloak that is exempt from the מצוה of ציצית
What? (asks for the meaning of something)

phrases.english: What is meant by an exempt cloak?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what one phrase in שמואל's ruling from step 14 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of garment is the 'exempt טלית' in שמואל's ruling?

steps.title: Maybe it is too small, but a ברייתא gives a small size limit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the exempt טלית is one too small to need ציצית. It then starts to challenge this from a ברייתא about a cloak big enough for a קטן to cover his head and most of his body.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is a cloak that does not have the required size, there is a difficulty. A ברייתא teaches: a cloak that is big enough for a child to cover his head and most of his body with it...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests one answer: the 'exempt' cloak is one that is too small to need ציצית. Right away it starts to attack that answer with a ברייתא about a cloak sized for a קטן, and the ברייתא continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that 'exempt' means the garment is under the size that requires ציצית. The ברייתא begins to set a fairly small size: enough for a child to cover his head and most of his body. The challenge will turn on what the ברייתא says about such a garment, and that part comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (offers a possible answer that is about to be challenged)
The required size (here, the size that makes a garment need ציצית)
A minor, a young child
His head and most of his body

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'exempt' here as meaning the garment is not a real garment at all. The question is only which reason makes this garment free from the מצוה of ציצית.

phrases.english: If we say it is one that does not have the required size,
but isn't it taught: a cloak that a child
can cover his head and most of his body with it
phrases.notes: The ברייתא keeps going on the next amud, where it tells us the הלכה for this cloak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to step 15's question and begins to attack it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the exempt טלית is one under the required size
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא sets the size limit at a cloak big enough for a child to cover his head and most of his body. The rest of the challenge comes on the next amud.
